original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: In the unsigned six-source characteristic-6 floor model, all 2280 endpoint pairs with unequal masks of the multiset (6,6,6,7,7,7) are realized by an explicit floor word that keeps that multiset at every s=4..18.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether one new connector operation has a favorable budget. This package keeps the unsigned dirty connector alphabet fixed and answers open question 1 of PR #7042: which unequal endpoint masks are joined by a monotone chain of this multiset. No signed bill is computed.
bottleneck_link: A missing unequal-mask chain would have been a diagonal obstruction inside type T1 that uses neither the (0, 9) hypothesis nor a frozen 12. Every such chain exists, so this multiset adds no further obstruction of that kind. The selected frontier stays 781451/250000000.
stop_rule: Stop after the ten orbit witnesses and the check of all 2280 transported words. Do not price a supplier and do not search the other five separation-3 families.
evidence: verify.py rechecks the endpoint domains, finds a 14-step path in each of the ten orbits, and checks the transported floor word on all 2280 unequal pairs. It prints PASS_C6_T1_UNEQUAL_MASK_CHAINS. Python 3.12, standard library only.
author: unpaidmoon
ai_assistance: Substantial Cursor Grok assistance. Independent human review and a proof-assistant proof are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: For one separation-3 family other than type T1, which unequal endpoint masks are joined by a monotone chain of that family's multiset?
open_questions.why_it_matters: T1 is the only one of the six families with no coordinate 12, and every unequal T1 pair now has a chain. A family that uses a 12 has a different legal step.
open_questions.first_step: Fix that family's multiset, write the legal exchange, and search one symmetry class of unequal masks.
open_questions.blocked_by: The step rule used here only exchanges a 6 with a 7. It does not apply to a coordinate equal to 12.
